subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 61-year-old woman with metastatic melanoma undergoes molecular testing of her tumor to detect a BRAF V600E mutation. The assay amplifies a guanine- and cytosine-rich exon of BRAF, and the laboratory must use a higher denaturation temperature for this amplicon than for the other amplicons in the same panel.
question: Which of the following best explains the higher denaturation temperature required for this GC-rich DNA fragment?

options.text: Guanine-cytosine pairs are held together by two hydrogen bonds each
Guanine-cytosine pairs are joined by covalent bonds between the bases
GC-rich DNA contains more deoxyribose per base pair
GC-rich DNA contains uracil instead of thymine
Each guanine-cytosine pair has three hydrogen bonds, so more energy is required to separate the strands

explanation_correct: Guanine and cytosine are joined by three hydrogen bonds, whereas adenine and thymine are joined by only two, so higher GC content raises the melting temperature of a DNA duplex. This is why GC-rich amplicons require a higher denaturation temperature in PCR-based tumor genotyping.

explanation_incorrect.A: G-C pairs have three hydrogen bonds; it is A-T pairs that have only two.
explanation_incorrect.B: Base pairing is noncovalent hydrogen bonding; covalent bonds occur within each base and along the sugar-phosphate backbone.
explanation_incorrect.C: The deoxyribose content per base pair is the same regardless of base composition, so it cannot explain a difference in melting temperature.
explanation_incorrect.D: Uracil is found in RNA, not DNA; DNA contains thymine.

educationalObjective: GC content raises the melting temperature of DNA because each G-C pair has three hydrogen bonds while each A-T pair has only two.
